steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease and flour two 9x5-inch loaf pans.
Whisk flour, flax seeds, cinnamon, salt, baking soda, baking powder, and arrowroot together in a bowl until evenly blended; set aside.
Whisk applesauce, white sugar, brown sugar, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract in a separate bowl until smooth. Fold in flour mixture and shredded zucchini until moistened.
Divide batter between the prepared loaf pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 70 minutes. Cool briefly in the pans before removing to cool completely on a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegan Zucchini Bread
raw_recipe.description: This vegan zucchini bread is made with simple baking ingredients, shredded zucchini, and applesauce for a deliciously moist and tender treat.
raw_recipe.name: Vegan Zucchini Bread

review.reviewBody: Followed recipe exactly and it turned out delicious and moist, not heavy at all. I may reduce sugar slightly next time, as it was a little too sweet for my taste, but overall a real winner!

I added to this recipe a little to make a vegan birthday cake for my daughter in law for her birthday. I didn't have any flax seeds, I used cornstarch instead of arrowroot powder. I added a 1/2 cup carob powder. I added 1/4 cup flour to adjust for high altitude. I baked it in a bundt pan and make a glaze with 1 cup powdered sugar, 2 tablespoons carob powder, a dash of vanilla and a tablespoon or so of almond milk. The cake baked up nice. Everyone at the birthday party said it was delish! There wasn't a crumb left over!

I can't make two loaves since I'm one person. I also had a 8x4 instead of 9x5 pan. I changed the serving size to half (12) and then 75% (9). Using 9 servings, I completely omitted the white sugar. I used coconut sugar, instead of brown sugar. I used vanilla almond milk, instead of vanilla. I used less than half of the oil required. I opted for the flax seed, but didn't use the arrowroot. Basically, I made the whole thing a lot healthier and it was delicious! I also adjusted the baking temp to 350 and cooked for less time (deeper pan). It was delicious! Thanks!

Instead of loaves, I wanted to make muffins to freeze and take to work as snacks. I had a couple of zucchini I needed to use, and this recipe turned out SO well! Delicious and moist! I used 2 c whole wheat flour and 1 c white, and substituted 3/4 c mashed banana for the oil. For muffins, I baked at 375 for 20 minutes and got my favorite vegan muffins yet! Thank you for this great recipe that proves you can bake beautifully without dairy products!!

Fantastic! I even reduced the oil by a little bit (2/3 cup vs 3/4) and adding in about a half cup of shredded dried coconut and it came out perfect. I made them into mini muffins (12 minutes in the oven) and regular cupcake-sized muffins (22 minutes). Next time I may even further reduce the oil to 1/2 cup and reduce the sugars to 2/3 cup each.

Absolutely delicious! I tweaked a little but did not feel it warranted any reduction of stars, because it was all based on personal preference. I cut back oil to 1/4 cup, increased apple sauce to 1 and 1/4 cups, and added in 1/4 cup sugar free maple syrup. I also reduced the white and brown sugars to 1/2 cup each, with the additional applesauce and maple making this *plenty* sweet and heartily scrumptious! No flax or arrowroot added, either, just more spices. Highly recommend!

I used a quarter cup less of flour and added in cocoa powder. I also added organic chocolate chips that are free from milk and egg products. It turned out very good but next time I will increase the applesauce a tiny bit!

This was very good. Added walnuts and made into muffins. I used coconut oil because that is what was on hand. Also, I recently stopped packing brown sugar to lighten things up a bit and it was still yummy-sweet. Baked for approximately 30 minutes.

i JUST finished this and am eating the warm bread right now- it's a new fave! i substituted half of the zucchini for shredded beets which was a first-time and it works well. i added 1/2 cup of cocoa to the recipe and that helped balance the earthy-ness of the beets. i only have one bread/loaf pan so i made half the batter into muffins- works well too.

This is a nice easy recipe but calls for way too much sugar & vanilla. I cut back to 1 1/2 cups of sugar and it was still too sweet. One cup sugar ( or less) would be plenty. Also recommend stirring the flour and zucchini as opposed to folding in and baking at 350 instead of 325. Batter baked unevenly at 325. Agree with previous comments that walnuts would make a nice addition. All said, its still a workable recipe.

I really love this zucchini bread, and it's always a hit when I make it. I do make several modifications though: I use extra virgin olive oil versus vegetable. I always use olive oil even with baking, I find that extra virgin olive oil is surprising subtle and works just fine baking sweet breads. Every time I make this I also lessen the sugar, I probably started it with about a cup of sugar, and then brought it down to 1/2 cup (equal ratio of brown to white sugar as the recipe calls for). This last time, I didn't use any sugar, and it came out tasting exactly the same to me-I say give it a try with less sugar. It will be a matter of taste, but you could easily cut half the sugar and it should be sweet enough. I find the applesauce is enough to sweeten it, and I do use some chocolate chips.. although I can vouch that it tastes sweet enough with the 1/2 cup of sugar even without the chocolate chips. Pecans are a nice addition to this as well. I would discourage using the full teaspoon of salt-it may be unnoticeable if you use a decent amount or the full amount of sugar that the recipe calls for. I made the mistake of putting the full teaspoon in with this last batch (no added sugar beyond the no sugar added applesauce), and I think it was way too salty. I'm kicking myself for not using just a pinch of sugar like I usually do.

We followed this recipe exactly but left out the optional ingredients (flax seed and arrowroot powder). This zucchini bread was wonderfully moist and cake like but not too sweet. A new family favorite for when we have extra zucchini to use up.
You get absolutely no health benefit from flax seeds unless they are ground. They are so tough that it's imposssible to chew them. I ground the seeds and made the bread and it was yummy.

I followed the recipe exactly as I rarely make vegan foods. This included the 3 tablespoons of flax seed. 😬 The bread was moist, sweet and tasty but the GI upset afterwards was not much fun. LOL. So, next try, NO FLAX SEEDS.

My picky teen son went back for seconds. Followed the recipe, but decreased the sugars by half, and included dark chocolate chunks. Future bakes, it'll be a quarter white sugar. Following one of the reviews, I topped the loaves with a sprinkling of brown sugar and chopped almonds before baking. Moist, crispy on top and the chopped almonds provided a nice crunch and texture. A buttered, perfectly spiced warm slice was so comforting on a cold rainy day. Thanks for sharing the recipe.

We enjoyed this bread! We did find it a bit too sweet so I reduced both the sugar and brown sugar by half. I also reduced the oil and used a 1/2 cup instead of 3/4 cup, and added a smashed banana for moisture. Additionally, we added a cup of chopped walnuts. Still tasted great! This is a recipe we will add to our rotation.
It doesn’t look very attractive in a world of large, fluffy loaves of bread, but it is definitely worth making (and eating). Deliciously moist with just the right amount of sweetness.

I missed having walnuts in my zucchini bread. I need some help with adding them to the recipe, and lessening the sugar some. I use raw sugar. For me the raisins are optional, but I would definitely prefer walnuts over the raisins. I loved the Zucchini Nut Bread that Paradise Bakery used to serve which had walnuts without the raisins.
Very yummy. I made this without arrowroot or flax seeds and it came out fine.
